source: Lowy Institute Poll — satisfaction with the direction of Australia

waves.method: Nationally representative fixed-line and mobile telephone survey by Social Research Centre, with state/territory quotas and call-back/appointment procedures to reach people away from home.
waves.sampleNote: A nationally representative sample of 1,200 Australian adults aged 18 and over.
waves.question: Overall, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in Australia today?
waves.sourceLabel: The 2017 Lowy Institute Poll: Overall, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in Australia today? Satisfied 47%; Dissatisfied 48%.

waves.method: Blended method: 600 online responses from Life in Australia (5–19 March) and 600 telephone responses (7–25 March), weighted and blended to preserve comparability with earlier telephone polls.
waves.sampleNote: 600 online respondents plus 600 telephone respondents, with dual-frame landline and mobile sampling and state/territory location quotas.
waves.question: Overall, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in Australia today?
waves.sourceLabel: The 2018 Lowy Institute Poll: Overall, are you satisfied or dissatisfied with the way things are going in Australia today? Satisfied 49%; Dissatisfied 46%.

$comment: National satisfaction by Lowy Institute, grouped with McKinnon's separately worded Satisfaction with the way Australia is heading and kept separate from Morgan's right-direction series and Ipsos' Global Average. 'Overall' and 'All things considered' are not identical wordings, so this is a separately labelled source, not a pooled observation. Other is the derived remainder for the combined Don't know / no view / neither category, never an independently measured neutral or Unsure share.
